title: Early Pandyas
capsule: The Early Pandyas were one of the three great Tamil crowned kingdoms of the Sangam period, ruling from their capital at Korkai (later Madurai) in the southernmost tip of the Indian subcontinent from at least the third century BCE. Their power rested on the pearl fisheries of the Gulf of Mannar and trade with Rome and the Hellenistic world, evidenced by Roman coins and Indo-Roman amphorae at Arikamedu. The greatest early Pandyan king, Nedunj Cheliyan III (Senguttuvan's contemporary, c. early 3rd cent. CE), is celebrated in Sangam poetry for his judicial impartiality. The early dynasty fades from record by the mid-fourth century CE, replaced by an obscure interregnum before the medieval Pandyas re-emerged in the sixth century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Pandyas' territorial extent in the Sangam period is only loosely reconstructed from poetry and later inscriptions; precise borders are unknown and the dataset polygon is necessarily approximate.
